title: Goal Decoupling
hook: Missing a revenue goal doesn't make you a failure. It makes you someone with new data.
statement: Keep who you are separate from the results you get.
explainer: When your self-worth is tied to a number, a bad month feels like a verdict on you. That makes it way harder to look at the result honestly and fix the plan.
sop: Name the result you've been treating as proof you're good enough.
Describe who you are by your habits, not by the number you hit.
Score your Identity Attachment to that result from 1 to 10.
After a miss, recommit to who you are first, then fix the plan.
Tie your self-talk to the process, especially right after a bad result.
equation_example: Identity Attachment 9. Stability = 10 minus 9 = 1. A bad result wrecks you. Drop it to 2 and Stability = 10 minus 2 = 8. Same bad result, it stings but it's not about you. Higher stability keeps setbacks as information, not identity threats.
question: Write down one outcome you've tied your self-worth to, then write who you are without it.
closing_statement: A bad result should cost you data, not your identity.
caption:
Principle Nº 238: Goal Decoupling

Missing a revenue goal doesn't make you a failure. It makes you someone with new data.

Keep who you are separate from the results you get.

Your turn: Write down one outcome you've tied your self-worth to, then write who you are without it.
